title: Software Supply-Chain Integrity Database — Overview and definition
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Dependency inventories, signatures, vulnerability advisories, and provenance records. The Software Supply-Chain Integrity Database guards the software you did not write: every dependency inventoried, every artifact signature-verified, every vulnerability advisory tracked, and provenance recorded from source to build. Modern applications are 90% third-party code — this database makes that 90% visible, verifiable, and continuously monitored, so a compromised package or a new CVE is found by the system, not by the breach.
capabilities: Dependency inventories: full transitive trees with versions and licenses
Signature verification: artifact signatures checked against publisher keys
Vulnerability advisory tracking: CVE feeds matched to inventory
Provenance records: SLSA-style build attestations per artifact
Policy engine: allow/deny/flag rules for dependency admission

title: Software Supply-Chain Integrity Database — Knowledge: technical reference
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Inventory: lockfiles pin exact versions; transitive closure computed from manifests; SBOM formats (SPDX, CycloneDX) standardize the inventory. Signatures: publisher signs artifact hashes; verification needs the publisher's public key via a trust root (Sigstore-style transparency logs). Vulnerabilities: CVE entries with severity (CVSS), affected version ranges; matching = version-in-range check against inventory. Provenance: SLSA levels — L1 (provenance exists), L2 (signed, tamper-evident), L3 (hardened builder); hermetic builds. Policy: deny known-critical CVEs, flag unsigned artifacts, require provenance above a threshold for production. Response: upgrade paths, patch windows, and the 'vulnerability is in a transitive dep' escalation procedure.

demo.code: function prop(a){const s=[...a].sort((x,y)=>x-y);const sorted=s.every((v,i)=>i===0||s[i-1]<=v);const perm=JSON.stringify([...a].sort((x,y)=>x-y))===JSON.stringify(s);return sorted&&perm;}let seed=42;function rnd(){seed=(seed*1103515245+12345)&0x7fffffff;return seed%100;}let pass=true;for(let t=0;t<200;t++){const a=Array.from({length:10},rnd);if(!prop(a)){pass=false;break;}}J({trials:200,pass});assert(pass,'property');

title: Software Supply-Chain Integrity Database — Verification: tests and limitations
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Tests: inventory test (transitive closure complete); signature test (tampered artifacts fail); CVE test (affected versions flagged, fixed versions clear); policy test (critical CVEs block). Limitations: advisory feeds lag real disclosure; private registries need their own feeds; signature trust roots must be configured. Every advisory carries published and last-checked dates.

demo.title: Execution: debugging signature match and bisection
demo.code: const sigs=[{re:/index out of range/i,cause:'off-by-one'},{re:/null|undefined/i,cause:'null-deref'}];const err='IndexError: list index out of range';const m=sigs.find(s=>s.re.test(err));const commits=['c1','c2','c3','c4','c5','c6','c7','c8'];const bad=5;let lo=0,hi=commits.length-1,steps=0;while(lo<hi){steps++;const mid=(lo+hi)>>1;if(mid>=bad)hi=mid;else lo=mid+1;}J({cause:m.cause,culprit:commits[lo],steps});assert(m.cause==='off-by-one'&&commits[lo]==='c6'&&steps===3,'debug');
